osaka_awa_sushi_minamisenba.notes: [Sushi · sushi omakase with a champagne pairing, Minami-Senba] A sophisticated ten-seat sushi counter inside a champagne-themed hotel near Nagahoribashi, built around one idea: sushi with champagne. The head chef, Kim, previously worked at the two-star Kuruma Sushi and at Sushi Shiro. The omakase runs to small dishes and about a dozen nigiri, with standouts like abalone steamed for six hours in its liver sauce (mixed with a little sushi rice at the end), sweet uni, medium-fatty tuna and anago with a rich sauce. The pairing pours a glass every two or three courses from a list of over 200 champagnes, with a featured house each month, and staff guide non-experts well. Dinner only, all guests start together; reserve for an anniversary night. One diner found a grilled fish watery.

chef_bio.background: Sushi counter in Cuvée J2 Hôtel Osaka (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The head chef, Kim, previously worked at the two-star Kuruma Sushi and at Sushi Shiro (April 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Sushi paired with champagne (2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "What stood out the most was the abalone that had been steamed for 6 hours. It was astonishingly tender, and when dipped in the liver sauce, the umami flavor burst forth…" — April 2026, Awa Sushi Omakase Course.
"I requested the champagne pairing, enjoying one glass with every two to three dishes, totaling five glasses." — April 2026.

osaka_furatto_curry_ya_inari.notes: [Curry · a ¥980 chicken katsu curry behind JR Namba, Inari] A small, warm curry shop on a quiet street about ten minutes from JR Namba that stays open through the afternoon. The order is the chicken katsu curry (¥980): the katsu is the surprise, crisp outside and tender and juicy within, over a mild, homestyle European curry sweet with onion. Some diners find the sauce a little sparse for the rice; there's a spicier curry too. It can be slow when one person is cooking at the lunch rush, smoking is allowed and the room gets hot in summer. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Curry shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "While the curry sauce itself wasn't particularly unique, the surprise came from the chicken katsu. The exterior was crispy, and the meat was tender, providing an excellent bite." — April 2026, Chicken Katsu Curry ¥980.
"The curry sauce is primarily sweet from the onions, with a very mild spiciness." — September 2026.

osaka_niku_teria_carne_bacca_kitahorie.notes: [Italian · a friendly Italian meat bar, Kitahorie] A stylish meat bar near Nishi-Ohashi that works for a solo glass at the counter or a group party at the tables. The signature is the slow-simmered beef tongue stew (¥2,600), tender enough to melt, with a baguette for the sauce; add the platter of chicken, pork and beef (¥2,280), the seared sirloin cap carpaccio and the homemade charcuterie, and finish with the butter rice topped with meat. Natto ajillo and a shungiku salad are unusual extras. Friendly staff; courses with two hours of drinks are ¥5,500. One diner found a group course thin and one had a Tabelog booking go unseen. Smoking allowed. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Italian meat bar (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The slowly simmered beef tongue is melt-in-your-mouth tender, and you'll want to add a baguette to soak up every drop of the sauce." — February 2026, Beef Tongue Stew ¥2,600.
"The standout dish was the Beef Sirloin Cap Carpaccio. It was a rare cut, seared over high heat…" — October 2026, all-you-can-drink course.

osaka_capo_classe_minamisenba.notes: [Italian · a one-person Italian with a ¥1,200 pasta lunch, Minami-Senba] A small second-floor Italian near Nagahoribashi, run single-handed and still quick, that fills up at lunch. The A Lunch (¥1,200) is the draw: a generous plate of the day's appetizers, such as a Spanish omelette and potato salad, warm homemade bread, then a pasta in your choice of tomato, oil or cream sauce, cooked firm from Italian dried pasta; the tuna and mushroom cream is a hit. Coffee is ¥100 more. At night, warm light from the windows and à la carte dishes like a caprese with blue cheese. Lunch is cash only; reserve. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Italian restaurant run by one person (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "For pasta, you can choose from three sauces: tomato, oil, or cream… The sauce, rich with fresh cream, was decadent yet light, making it very enjoyable." — January 2026, A Lunch ¥1,200, tuna and mushroom cream sauce.
"It's impressive how efficiently… everything [is managed] with just one person on duty, and I didn't feel like I was waiting at all." — August 2026, oil pasta.

Weekday lunch is soup curry only; dinner is mushroom cuisine only; some lunch days serve the course — see Instagram (Tabelog). Reserve for dinner (September 2026). Cards accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_kinoko_no_sato_minamisenba.notes: [Mushroom · creative mushroom courses, Minami-Senba] A small, pleasant restaurant near Shinsaibashi where nearly everything at dinner is mushrooms. The Bamboo course runs from mushroom sashimi (crunchy yet moist, several kinds) and a shiitake dobin-mushi through grilled mushrooms and tempura to a hot pot crowded with varieties, then a risotto made in the broth and ice cream. Staff explain the mushrooms and how to eat each dish. Seasoning is gentle and the umami is deep. Try the mushroom sake or gin. Weekday lunch is a different menu: soup curry only. Reserve for dinner. One diner got soggy tempura.

chef_bio.background: Mushroom-themed restaurant (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "I had never tried sashimi made with mushrooms before, and the crunchy yet moist texture with various types was a refreshing experience." — October 2026.
"The shiitake dobin mushi was especially amazing—I could drink it for a lifetime!" — September 2026.

osaka_curry_ya_dekkao_minamisenba.notes: [Curry · Sri Lankan-style curry plates, Minami-Senba] A busy, homey second-floor curry shop near Shinsaibashi, easy to miss from the street, serving Sri Lankan-style curry adapted to Japanese tastes: spicy but approachable. Build a plate around the bone-in chicken curry and one or two of the four or five daily curries, such as clam and tomato or spicy coconut tuna; the Dekkao Special is ¥1,300 and the Greedy version adds a second curry and more sides for ¥1,650. Taste each curry and side first, then mix it all together. Warm, smiling staff. Expect a line at opening. Mostly lunch; dinner Tuesdays and Thursdays. Closed Sundays. PayPay, no cards.

chef_bio.background: Sri Lankan-style curry shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Sri Lankan curry blended with Japanese cooking to suit Japanese tastes (September 2026 review, citing the owner).

anecdotes.text: "The standard way to enjoy this meal is to first savor each curry and side dish separately, and then mix them together." — September 2026, Greedy Dekkao Special ¥1,650.

"The clam and tomato curry, which I tried for the first time, had a wonderful clam flavor and was delicious. It was perfectly spicy, and it paired well with the chicken curry." — September 2026, Dekkao Special ¥1,300.

osaka_amber_kitahorie.notes: [Italian · a bright, casual Italian bistro, Kitahorie] A bright, warm Italian in western Kitahorie, a short walk from Yotsubashi, casual enough for families at lunch and lively at dinner. Lunch is pasta with potage, bread and salad, such as a fresh tomato pasta with swordfish and spinach. At night, courses and à la carte run to braised beef cheek, a rich uni cream pasta for mopping up with baguette, melt-in-the-mouth black-haired wagyu, sirloin cap steak and crab risotto, ending with homemade tiramisu. Birthday plates on request; friendly staff. It fills up, so reserve. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Italian bistro (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The braised beef cheek was incredibly tender, and the uni cream pasta was rich and paired perfectly with the baguette." — September 2026, course.
"I had the fig butter baguette, crab risotto, and sirloin cap steak. Everything was absolutely delicious." — October 2026.

osaka_sushi_kazenogi_minamisenba.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish and shellfish omakase with beef and egg dishes.
osaka_sushi_kazenogi_minamisenba.hours_raw: Two seatings daily, 18:00–20:00 and 21:00–23:30; irregular closings and New Year break (Tabelog). Omakase ¥28,000 (February 2026). Cash only — no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). Gold leaf can be left off on request (March 2026).
osaka_sushi_kazenogi_minamisenba.notes: [Sushi · a six-seat omakase with a gold-leaf finale, Minami-Senba] A quiet, six-seat sushi counter near Nagahoribashi with two seatings a night. The chef talks fluently with overseas guests in each guest’s own language. It's known online for its show-stopping finale, uni served on the back of your hand under a shower of gold leaf, but diners who came for the photos stay for the food: delicate starters, homemade karasumi, a cod roe chawanmushi and nigiri like kuruma shrimp, fugu milt and charcoal-grilled saba bozushi, on slightly soft rice. The omakase was ¥28,000 in early 2026. Hospitality is warm and humble, with humor at the counter. Gold leaf can be skipped if you're heading to work. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Sushi omakase counter (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The chef talks fluently with overseas guests in each guest’s own language (February 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "One standout was the 'Saba Bōzushi' (mackerel sushi) grilled with charcoal. The combination of the fragrant charcoal aroma and the rich flavor of the mackerel was exceptional…" — May 2026.
"…upon entering, I was pleasantly surprised by the calm ambiance and the warm hospitality… The sushi rice was slightly softer than usual…" — March 2026.

osaka_uwo_u_kitahorie.notes: [Eel · an eel counter since 1946, Kitahorie] A small counter near Nishi-Ohashi that has grilled eel since 1946, Edo style: steamed so the eel is fluffy, then finished over Kishu Binchotan with a sauce kept since the start, light and only gently sweet. A mother and son run it: the owner's son, the third generation, has taken over the grill. The unadon (¥1,800, half an eel) is the everyday order, and the premium unaju (¥3,600) or the Gomori-ju with grilled liver go further; you'll be asked whether you want sansho. Weekday Kimagure lunches are a bargain: a chicken katsu don from ¥700 that overflows the bowl. Eel is grilled to order. Expect crowds around Doyo no Ushi. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Eel restaurant run by two people (Tabelog; 2023–2026 reviews). A mother and son run it: the owner's son, the third generation, has taken over the grill (July 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Sauce kept since the restaurant opened (2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The eel is grilled using Kishu Binchotan charcoal, following the Edo-style (Kanto-style). The tender meat is coated in a sauce that has been passed down since the restaurant's inception." — April 2026, Gomori Ju ¥2,200.
"Since it's steamed, the meat is quite fluffy. The surface is grilled to a crisp, giving it a nice char…" — October 2026, premium unaju ¥3,600.

osaka_la_golosetta_minamisenba.notes: [Pizza · wood-fired pizza in a little house, Minami-Senba] A charming small house near Nagahoribashi with an Italian wood-fired oven at the back, a counter downstairs and tables upstairs, and a stained-glass pizza in the window. Pizzas come out in minutes with a chewy, fragrant crust whose twisted edge is a highlight. The Diavola (¥1,300), a cheese-free marinara with spicy salami, chili and plenty of garlic, is properly hot, so ask for it milder if you like; the Bianca with porcini and smoked mozzarella and the Quattro Formaggi are the cheesy picks. Lunch pizzas come with a salad for about ¥1,000–1,300. Go before noon. Closed Mondays.

anecdotes.text: "The twisted edge has a nice chewiness and a wonderful wheat aroma, the dough itself is very delicious." — August 2026, Diavola ¥1,300.
"I ordered the Bianca Porcini, and as expected from a wood-fired oven, it was served in just a few minutes! The aroma of smoked mozzarella and porcini mushrooms was irresistible!" — August 2026.

osaka_tamaki_minamisenba.notes: [Japanese · monthly fish hot-pot course with a sake pairing, Minami-Senba] A small, long-running izakaya tucked into the back of a building near Shinsaibashi, with a counter and a few tables. The draw is the monthly course, around ¥5,000 with a glass of sake matched to each dish: a seasonal starter, three kinds of sashimi, grilled and steamed fish, then a fish hot pot as the main, such as Kinmedai shabu-shabu or conger eel sukiyaki, finished with zosui or noodles. The menu changes every month; one diner returns every month. Dislikes are handled if you say so when booking. Weekday lunch is a cheap daily set. Smoking allowed. Closed Sundays.

osaka_lemone_minamisenba.notes: [French · a late-night creative French bistro, Minami-Senba] A cozy counter-and-table French spot near Nagahoribashi that serves until 1:00, with warm service and a sommelier chef for wine. osaka_sake_pan_tsutsumi_minamisenba.notes: [Bar · a bread-and-drinks bar, Minami-Senba] A stylish little second-floor bar near Nagahoribashi built around bread with wine. Wines sit in a fridge for you to choose, from ¥3,800 a bottle including domestic labels, plus craft gin and grape beer. With one person on the floor it can be slow. Cash only. Open late Fridays and Saturdays; closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

osaka_bokkake_ya_shinmachi.notes: [Soba · a soba shop that turns into a soba izakaya, Shinmachi] A small soba shop near Yotsubashi that has served thin, fragrant Ju-wari soba for many years, packed at lunch and a relaxed soba izakaya at night. At lunch, try the Iso Karami Soba with seaweed, sudachi and spicy daikon, or a set of cold soba with a miso tempura rice bowl; the grated daikon is fiercely hot, and the soba is good with just salt. In the evening, order the five-piece small-plate platter, a dashi omelette and grilled iwana with sake, then finish with Bokkake soba. Counter seats are tight. Closed Sundays.

anecdotes.text: "The dish was beautifully presented with plenty of seaweed and slices of sudachi arranged like a floral pattern, topped with spicy daikon radish." — October 2026, Iso Karami Soba.

"I tried it first with salt. Delicious! It paired perfectly. The salt really enhanced the flavor of the soba itself… What surprised me was the grated daikon! It was incredibly spicy…" — October 2026, grated soba and miso tempura rice bowl set.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: ぼっかけや、大阪市西区新町1-2-13 新町ビル 1F、四ツ橋駅北1A出口・本町駅から徒歩3分、月〜土 11:30〜14:30 (L.O. 料理14:00)・17:30〜22:00 (L.O. 料理21:30)、祝日は21:30まで、日曜休み、祝日の休みは Tabelog か Instagram で、カード・PayPay 可、20席 (カウンター5)。口コミ(2008年〜2026年10月): 昼は混む小さなそば店、夜はそば居酒屋、細く香りのいい Ju-wari のそば、塩で食べてもおいしい、ぼっかけそば、Iso Karami Soba (海藻、sudachi、辛い大根おろし)、冷たいoroshi-bukkake (大根おろしがとても辛い)、Yamato Tororo Soba 1,450円、くるみのそば、昼はそばと味噌の天丼 (ごぼうの天ぷら) のセット、Nozawana のおにぎり、夜は小皿5種盛り、だしの卵焼き、豆、iwana の塩焼き、おまかせの酒の肴、コース、Daishinshu・Igarashi などの日本酒、Yona Yona Ale、カウンターは狭い。

osaka_stylish_grill_tyu_hakurocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: beef hamburg steak; beef-tendon soup; egg rice.
osaka_stylish_grill_tyu_hakurocho.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu–Sun and public holidays 11:00–15:30 (last order 15:00); closed Wed (Tabelog). Lines at weekday lunch; before opening or after 14:00 is easiest (September 2026). PayPay only — no cards or e-money (Tabelog).
osaka_stylish_grill_tyu_hakurocho.notes: [Hamburg steak · a seven-seat hamburg steak lunch, Hakurocho] A tiny lunch-only grill in the Senba textile district with a line most weekdays. The hamburg steak is coarse-ground, seared crisp on a sizzling iron plate and juicy inside, roughly 150–200 g; top it with wasabi grated daikon (one repeat diner's usual order), cheese, bacon or a tangy homemade tomato sauce, in Japanese or demi-glace style. Pay ¥100 more for egg rice made with rich Ran-oh eggs. Rice and a ginger beef-tendon soup are refillable. Friendly staff. Arrive before opening or after 2 pm. PayPay only. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Hamburg steak lunch spot (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "This hamburg steak has a coarsely ground texture that gives it a satisfying meatiness, crumbling delightfully in my mouth." — August 2026, bacon hamburg steak +70 g with egg rice.
"The wasabi adds a nice touch, making it refreshing and enhancing the flavors of the meat and fat." — September 2026, Wasabi Oroshi Hamburger Steak with Egg Rice.

osaka_no_29_shinmachi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: soy-based yakiniku sauces and sukiyaki; ponzu.
osaka_no_29_shinmachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a butcher and beef restaurant.
osaka_no_29_shinmachi.hours_raw: Meat counter 11:30–20:00; lunch 11:30–14:30 (last order 13:30); kappo course dinner by reservation only, two sittings 18:00–20:00 and 20:30–22:30; irregular closings (Tabelog). 10% service charge at dinner (Tabelog). Cards and PayPay accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_no_29_shinmachi.notes: [Yakiniku · a butcher's back-room yakiniku kaiseki, Shinmachi] Walk past the meat counter of this butcher near Nishi-Ohashi to a heavy door and an eight-seat chef's table. Dinner is a reserved meat kaiseki: appetizers, smoked yukke spooned over ikura rice, grilled liver and sukiyaki, then yakiniku of strip loin, tongue and the much-praised harami, cooked and explained in front of you. Two sittings a night; 10% service. Lunch is a simpler way in: a thick, tender harami steak set (¥1,580) with refillable rice and soup, though one diner found lunch service inattentive and the extra sauces cost ¥150.

chef_bio.origin: Osaka branch of a yakiniku business from Ehime (May 2024 review).
chef_bio.background: Butcher and yakiniku kaiseki counter (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "As you head towards the back of the butcher shop, you'll find a heavy door leading to the chef's table." — August 2026.

"Every single meat dish was delicious, and the staff provided thorough explanations, making it easy to understand. It was exciting to see the cooking done right in front of me." — September 2026, dinner.

osaka_pizzeria_da_tigre_shinmachi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a pizza-only menu; wheat dough.
osaka_pizzeria_da_tigre_shinmachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: cheese on most pizzas; the Marinara is the usual cheese-free Neapolitan pizza — ask.
osaka_pizzeria_da_tigre_shinmachi.hours_raw: Wed, Fri, Sat, Sun 11:30–14:30 and 17:00–21:00; Thu 11:30–14:30; closed Mon–Tue (Tabelog). No reservations; ticket machine; cash only (2026 reviews; Tabelog). Lines at weekend lunch (April 2026). Takeout too (September 2026).
osaka_pizzeria_da_tigre_shinmachi.notes: [Pizza · a one-person Neapolitan pizza counter, Shinmachi] A clean, thirteen-seat counter near Nishi-Ohashi where the owner, working solo as pizzaiolo, stretches, tops and fires every pizza in a blazing wood oven in front of you, alongside a steady run of takeout orders. It has held a Michelin Bib Gourmand five years running, was ranked 27th in 50 Top Pizza Asia-Pacific 2023, and was named one of the top 100 pizza restaurants in 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2021. Buy a ticket from the machine; the Margherita is ¥1,000 and arrives in a few minutes, toasted outside and chewy within, uncut so you slice it yourself. Try the Marinara or the Ricotta e Cipolla too. No reservations and cash only; go right at opening, as lunch lines form fast. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Neapolitan pizzeria run by one person (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The owner works solo, stretching dough non-stop (September 2026 review). It has held a Michelin Bib Gourmand five years running, was ranked 27th in 50 Top Pizza Asia-Pacific 2023, and was named one of the top 100 pizza restaurants in 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2021 (September 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The counter seating allows you to closely watch the skilled pizzaiolo at work, which is a real treat. The way… the dough [is stretched]… is mesmerizing." — September 2026, Margherita ¥1,000.
"The paper bag containing my fork and knife had notes on why the pizza isn't served pre-sliced and tips on the best way to enjoy it…" — September 2026.

osaka_goyakura_minamisenba.vegan_detail: Not vegan: beef, pork and chicken curries made with dashi.
osaka_goyakura_minamisenba.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Fri about 11:30–15:00; Sat, Sun and public holidays about 12:00–15:00; closed Wed–Thu (Tabelog). Wait for the owner to take your order (September 2026). Rice can take about 10 minutes at times (October 2026). Cash only (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (Tabelog).
osaka_goyakura_minamisenba.notes: [Curry · a one-person dashi curry shop, Minami-Senba] A calm, lunch-only curry counter behind a heavy door in Minami-Senba, where the owner cooks alone and calls the style "Ware": thick curries built on Japanese dashi, aromatic rather than hot. Try the Japanese Chicken Keema with daikon, the miso-rich Beef & Pork Mara, or the tomato Goyakura Keema, and ask for a combination even though it isn't on the menu; the super-spicy chicken keema is for heat seekers. Four pickles sit on the side. House rule: wait for your order to be taken. Cash only; smoking allowed. Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays.

chef_bio.background: Curry shop run by one person (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Calls its own dashi-based curries "Ware" (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The umami from the ingredients, combined with the dashi, elevates the flavor, creating a unique taste that doesn't quite fit into the categories of European or spice curry." — September 2026, Special Beef Ware ¥1,500.
"True to its name, the moment I took a bite, the flavor of the dashi was incredible! It even had daikon radish in it…" — October 2026, Japanese Chicken Keema.

Dinner cover ¥400 per person (Tabelog). One drink per person with the lunch course (October 2026). Cards and PayPay accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_italy_zoo_minamisenba.notes: [Italian · a small Italian with animals hidden in the décor, Minami-Senba] A gentle, café-like twelve-seat Italian at the back of a building near Nagahoribashi, with antique furniture, dried flowers and little animals hidden everywhere, even on the door handles. The chef honed the craft at Michelin-starred restaurants in Italy. Lunch is excellent value: the ¥1,300 weekday set brings a plate of seven carefully made vegetable appetizers and a mini soup before a well-judged pasta, and the ¥3,200 course adds a main such as braised Chami pork. Dinner is a course of about eleven small, elaborate dishes, explained one by one, from homemade ham to straw-grilled wagyu; desserts cost extra and portions are small. Closed Thursdays.

chef_bio.background: Italian restaurant (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews). The chef honed the craft at Michelin-starred restaurants in Italy (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "As the name suggests, various animals are hidden throughout the restaurant. Even the door handles feature animal designs." — December 2025, 11-dish course.
"The vegetable appetizers were served in small portions, with seven varieties!" — July 2026, weekday A Set ¥1,300.

osaka_dish_curry_relish_minamisenba.notes: [Curry · weekly spice-curry plates, Minami-Senba] A seven-seat curry counter near Nagahoribashi run by one person, open straight through from lunch into the evening, which makes it a good late lunch. Order the three-curry assorted plate (¥1,500): the curries change weekly, but two diners singled out the dry keema with its numbing, Sichuan-pepper tingle, alongside choices like squid tentacle with basil or a potato curry, all with a fried egg and three crisp pickles to mix in. Spices are well balanced rather than fiery. Check Instagram for the week's menu. Cash only. Closed Sundays and Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Spice curry counter run by one person (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "…the keema curry… had a numbing sensation like Sichuan pepper and paired perfectly with the fried egg." — April 2026, assorted platter of three, ¥1,500.
"The menu seems to change weekly, so I recommend checking… Instagram before you go!" — July 2026.

osaka_wai_sai_ikutamacho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: fish-centred set meals and courses with dashi.
osaka_wai_sai_ikutamacho.hours_raw: Mon, Thu–Sun 11:30–15:00 (last order 14:00) and 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:00); closed Tue–Wed (Tabelog). Dishes take time; relax and wait (September 2026). Cards and PayPay accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_wai_sai_ikutamacho.notes: [Japanese · seafood lunches and courses in a renovated house, Ikutamacho] A beautifully renovated house on a quiet street near Tanimachi 9-chome, with a counter and tables. Lunch is a choice of grilled or simmered fish, the species a surprise, with side dishes and refillable rice for ¥1,650; the simmered fish is generous and gently seasoned. At night, the ¥5,500 course runs from appetizers and fine sashimi through a dobin-mushi brightened with sudachi and a whole simmered fish to tempura and clay-pot rice, closing with nyumen. Everything is made with care, so it takes time; settle in. Closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Japanese seafood restaurant (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "I had the option to choose between grilled fish or simmered fish, so I ordered the simmered fish set meal… The simmered fish was Houbou, and it was tender and flavorful with a light taste." — October 2026, lunch ¥1,650.
"The clay pot was filled with fragrant broth… and then added a squeeze of sudachi for a refreshing burst of flavor…" — October 2026, ¥5,500 course.

osaka_shinmachi_curry.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:00–16:00; closed Sun; irregular closings (Tabelog). Shrimp curry Thu–Sat only (March 2026). Cash only (Tabelog; September 2026). Opened around August 2025; first anniversary in 2026 (reviews).
osaka_shinmachi_curry.notes: [Curry · dashi-based spice curry, Shinmachi] A small curry counter under a green awning in Shinmachi, run by a couple whose bright, attentive service, remembering returning faces, is half the appeal. The owner was formerly manager of a very famous Osaka curry shop that had a Bib Gourmand. The curry is light and soupy, built on dashi rather than heat: choose a chicken-broth base with Shodoshima soy sauce or a katsuobushi dashi with soy milk, then chicken-and-pork or fish keema, and mix in the sides, such as a crunchy gizzard achar. Add the ¥200 squid and clam Thai curry if it's on. Shrimp curry Thursdays to Saturdays. Open through 4 pm, handy for a late lunch. Cash only. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Spice curry shop run by two people (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews). A couple runs it; the owner was formerly manager of a very famous Osaka curry shop that had a Bib Gourmand (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The umami of the Japanese-style dashi is irresistible, and I couldn't help but keep eating." — October 2026, Rich Beef and Pork Keema (Japanese-style dashi) with cilantro.
"Among them, the gizzard achar stands out with its satisfying crunch and is absolutely exquisite." — September 2026, fish keema + sides ¥1,450.

osaka_saka_song_shinmachi.notes: [Izakaya · a friendly late-night izakaya of Japanese and Thai small plates, Shinmachi] A cozy, sticker-and-poster-covered izakaya tucked into the back of a building near Nishi-Ohashi, open until 2 am, where a friendly owner makes newcomers feel as welcome as the crowd of returning customers. Plates are small and cheap, so solo diners can try several: a nutty yam woon sen heaped with cilantro, salt-grilled chicken cartilage, mushrooms in anchovy butter, corn tempura. Finish with the khao soi, rich coconut soup with crispy noodles, and add rice to the last of the broth. Cash only; smoking allowed. Closed Sundays.

osaka_yakiniku_union_shinmachi.notes: [Yakiniku · a stylish wagyu yakiniku with fresh offal, Shinmachi] An eleven-seat yakiniku near Nishi-Ohashi with a stylish room and charming staff, where one diner reported eating well for about ¥10,000 and feeling light afterwards. Start raw with the wagyu yukke or harami sashimi yukke, then grill the tender special harami, lean cuts and thick tongue, and don't skip the fresh offal, such as heart, mino and kori kori. Unsure? Ask for the chef's platter and say lean or rib. The wagyu chiritori hot pot, packed with vegetables, is a cold-night alternative, and the thin, sweet-sour cold noodles make a good finish. Closed Tuesdays.

osaka_prestau_shinmachi.notes: [Italian · a refined Italian of seasonal courses, Shinmachi] A calm twelve-seat Italian near Nishi-Ohashi, pale blue outside and gray stone and concrete within, where courses of unexpected ingredient pairings arrive on carefully chosen tableware. The chef has 20 years in Italian cooking, and one diner says the chef came out of Ponte Vecchio; the owner is a certified sommelier who picks the monthly sake pairings. The chef trained at a well-known restaurant in Kobe and runs PRESTAU with the chef's wife. The monthly lunch course (¥7,700) is the way in: a squid-ink risotto with cuttlefish and sudachi, delicate sardine with turnip, homemade conchiglie in beef-tongue ragù and charcoal-grilled duck, with a delicate rather than bold hand on seasoning. Desserts come in three stages. Dislikes are handled if mentioned ahead. One diner found drink service slow. Closed Mondays and one Sunday a month.

osaka_raamen_hareruya_daikokucho.notes: [Ramen · rich chicken paitan by Daikokucho Station] A friendly ramen shop seconds from Daikokucho Station, open since late 2024 with a table for four as well as the counter. The young owner has a great smile, and a lively head chef works alongside. The signature is a rich, frothy chicken paitan; the special bowl adds grilled chashu, steamed chicken, an egg and red onion. The paitan also comes as a miso ramen, light enough to finish, and there's a back-fat shoyu with thin tip menma that is lighter than it looks. The mazesoba (¥1,250) comes with a rice bowl of aburi chashu. One diner found the miso broth lukewarm. Open all day at weekends.

osaka_noodleya_mechakucha_shinmachi.notes: [Ramen · tom yum noodles and porcini ramen, Shinmachi] A one-person, eight-seat lunch shop in western Shinmachi with ramen unlike anywhere else. The Tom Yum Noodles (¥990) are the draw: creamy, sour, spicy and savory at once, with a mound of cilantro over straight noodles. The porcini mushroom salt ramen has its own fans, and there are dan dan noodles, a sudachi shoyu ramen and tsukemen. Add a small green curry or rice bowl. Cash only, and the ticket machine wants coins or older ¥1,000 notes, so bring change. Lunch only; closed Sundays, with the odd surprise closure.

osaka_hao_zaimokucho.notes: [Ramen · a chashu-heavy neighborhood ramen shop, Zaimokucho] A small, old-fashioned ramen counter near Matsuyamachi, now under a new owner and busy even mid-afternoon. The draw is chashu: the chashu ramen (¥1,200–1,300) carries about five thick, tender slices over thin, soft noodles, in shio, shoyu or miso, with garlic and spicy miso on the counter to sharpen it. For something different, the Harapeko Kizuna-men is a bowl of mixed noodles with chopped chashu and green onion; mix it from the bottom, then add vinegar and chili oil as the owner suggests. The garlic-chive gyoza are worth adding. One diner found the broth lukewarm. Cash only; open all day; closed Sundays.

osaka_aburasoba_a_minamihonmachi.notes: [Abura-soba · cheap abura-soba with a wall of condiments, Minami-Honmachi] A tiny eight-seat abura-soba shop near Sakaisuji-Honmachi where a simple bowl starts around ¥500. osaka_taiwan_ramen_kun_nipponbashi.notes: [Ramen · cheap Taiwanese ramen and mazesoba in Den Den Town] A simple ticket-machine noodle shop on a side street of Den Den Town, with a counter downstairs and more seats upstairs. The Taiwanese ramen is a bargain at ¥750: a soy-sauce broth that grows richer as the spicy minced meat seeps in, over thin noodles with good bite, milder than the chain versions and adjustable up to super spicy. The mazesoba comes with minced meat, onion and crunchy peanuts, with free fried onions on the table and rice offered at the end. Not into heat? There's a gentle tonkotsu ramen. Large size is free. Cash only. Open every day.

osaka_ramen_kakumei_minamisenba.notes: [Ramen · aged-shoyu ramen five ways, Minami-Senba] A bright, roomy ramen shop near Nagahoribashi, open since early 2024, with tables as well as a counter and a family-friendly feel. The house bowl is aged shoyu ramen on a chicken-and-seafood broth, in five styles: plain, with katsuo, with yuzu (¥900), with back fat, or black. The back-fat versions are lighter than they look, and the spicy garlic chives on the table give them a punch. There's also an iekei-style tonkotsu and a thick tantanmen, plus seasonal specials such as a chilled ago-dashi ramen with duck chashu in summer. Ticket machine, cash only; staff are lively and quick.

osaka_kuse_ga_tsuyoi_menya_reiwa_hakuroc.notes: [Ramen · a JoJo-themed performance ramen counter, Hakurocho] Less a ramen shop than an attraction: nine counter seats in a room filled with figures from JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, where the owner drains noodles shouting the manga's catchphrases and serves each bowl in character. Every ramen is ¥2,000 with free extra noodles and toppings; the miso tonkotsu is rich and creamy, the cilantro ramen very strong, and the tomato mazesoba (¥1,500) comes with free rice, cheese and kimchi. A ¥1,000 prize lottery never loses. Groups are served in turn, so expect to queue one to two hours from before 7 pm. Cash only. Closed Sundays and Mondays.

osaka_ajinomoto_malatang_motomachi.notes: [Malatang · a sesame-rich malatang worth the walk, Motomachi] A pick-your-own malatang shop between Namba and Daikokucho, a little out of the way, so there's rarely a queue. Fill a bowl from the case of individually priced ingredients, from napa cabbage, okra and lotus root to egg tofu, quail eggs and beef, choose your noodles, from instant to chewy thick ones, then set the numbing and spice levels separately. The broth is unusually rich in sesame, closer to dan dan noodles, and a splash of the black vinegar halfway through makes it creamier. A bowl typically runs ¥1,200–1,700. Pay after eating. Open daily until 11 pm.

osaka_sakanaya_uotachi_shinmachi.notes: [Seafood · a fishmonger's lunch counter, Shinmachi] A fish shop in western Shinmachi with a surprisingly roomy counter at the back, where lunch is a good-value seafood meal. The daily sashimi bowl comes heaped with tuna on red-vinegar rice, and the Hokkaido bowl piles salmon, ikura, scallops and crab, each with two side dishes, a rich fish soup and dessert for about ¥1,400. There's an eight-piece sushi set too. Evenings bring a long list of fish dishes and good sashimi. Buy fish, side dishes or a bento on the way out. Closed Wednesdays and the 1st and 3rd Tuesdays.

osaka_yakitori_okibi_senba.notes: [Yakitori · aged-chicken yakitori by night, chicken ramen by day, Senba] A quiet, hidden-feeling yakitori counter in the basement of the Senba Center Building, a minute from Honmachi Station. At night it grills Banshu Akadori aged for five days, one skewer at a time: start with the thigh-and-breast tataki to taste the difference, then negima, breast and well-seasoned tsukune, with side dishes like crab miso and cream cheese, liver simmered with sansho, and an oyakodon to close. At lunch the kitchen turns its chicken broth into ramen: a creamy chicken paitan with pork and chicken chashu (¥1,450) or a black-sesame dan dan noodle. Friendly, attentive staff. Closed Sundays.

osaka_kaede_udon_tempura_shinmachi.notes: [Udon · udon-and-tempura set meals, Shinmachi] A clean, modern Japanese udon shop in Shinmachi that opened in August 2026 and fills with office workers at lunch. Order the Irodori Mamezara Gozen: pick one of seven udon, from sudachi to a meaty curry udon, and three tempura made to order, two pieces each, with plump shrimp, sweet corn and a big aji fry among the choices, plus a tray of small side dishes, chilled tofu and pickles, from ¥1,500. Or keep it cheap with zaru udon, à la carte tempura and rice balls. Evening hours Friday and Saturday only. One diner was squeezed onto a small table. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Udon and tempura restaurant (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "You can choose from an impressive 7 types of udon (Kamatama, Meat, Sudachi, Curry, etc.)!… The freshly fried, crispy shrimp tempura, squid tempura, and kakiage were all hearty portions." — October 2026, set meal.

"It comes with three side dishes, chilled tofu, pickles, and a choice of three tempura for JPY 1800. By the way, if you choose kake udon or zaru udon, you can enjoy all of this for just JPY 1500…" — October 2026.

osaka_savatomy_azuchimachi.notes: [Chinese · a creative Chinese bar of small plates, Azuchimachi] A stylish, busy Chinese bar near Sakaisuji-Honmachi where colorful small plates are sized for two to share. The must-order is the seared bonito in the house red sauce, smoky and gently spicy; add the moist drool chicken, fluffy anago, dim sum and, in season, oyster spring rolls, with an 18-year Shaoxing wine, straight or with soda. Seasoning is balanced enough for friends who avoid heat. Lunch is a bargain, with dan dan noodles, mapo tofu or a fuller set for about ¥2,000; one weekday it was full soon after 11:30. Reserve for dinner. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Creative Chinese restaurant and bar (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Seared bonito with red sauce; small Chinese plates.

anecdotes.text: "The first bite of the seared bonito was shocking. It was unlike any seared bonito I had ever tasted before. The smoky aroma and slightly spicy flavor were incredible." — October 2026, lunch.
"Each dish was perfectly portioned for sharing between two people, allowing us to enjoy a variety of menu items in small bites." — October 2026.

osaka_men_chu_minamihorie.notes: [Ramen · an old-style chicken shoyu shop, Minami-Horie] A quiet neighborhood ramen shop in western Minami-Horie with warm, attentive staff. The bowls are light and old-fashioned: a chicken shoyu broth that tastes mild at first and deepens as the tare at the bottom mixes in, medium-thin straight noodles, and tender, well-marinated chashu and good menma, which even diners who found the soup lacking praise. The Horie Ramen (¥930) is the house bowl, and a small fried rice (¥420) makes a cheap set. Reviews are split on the broth, so come for something gentle. Open late; closed Mondays. Cash only.

anecdotes.text: "At first sip, the broth seemed a bit light, but as I continued eating, the flavor intensified. This was likely due to the tare that had settled at the bottom of the bowl mixing in." — July 2026, chicken shoyu ramen ¥770.
"The chashu was tender and well-marinated, making it delicious." — September 2026, Horie Ramen.

osaka_ganbare_hourai_minamihorie.notes: [Ramen · a cozy chicken-paitan ramen and Chinese-food spot, Minami-Horie] A café-like ramen and Chinese-food shop facing Takadaibashi Park; one diner has ordered takeout from it for years. The chicken paitan comes in shio or shoyu, rich but not heavy, with a seasoned egg included at no charge, thick melt-in-the-mouth chashu, chopped onion and fried garlic. Pair a half bowl (¥800) with the fluffy small fried rice (¥350) for a cheap loop of rice, soup and chashu. There are also dan dan noodles, Taiwanese mazesoba, gyoza and a long drinks list. Smoking allowed. Hours vary; check before going.

osaka_shuki_lanzhou_namba.notes: [Lanzhou noodles · hand-pulled Lanzhou beef noodles and lamb skewers, Namba-naka] A big, no-frills Chinese noodle house between Namba and Daikokucho. An older review found staff and customers mostly of Chinese descent. The draw is hand-pulled Lanzhou beef noodles in a light, spiced beef-bone broth finished with chili oil and cilantro, with your pick of eight noodle widths, chewy almost like udon at the wide end; Set A (¥1,200) adds small side dishes. Add cumin-spiced lamb skewers, or try the sour-and-spicy vermicelli and a cheap lamb-with-cumin set. Splash in the table vinegar halfway. Open every day. Ask for the non-smoking section.

osaka_ramen_hana_shinmachi.notes: [Ramen · truffle-scented chicken paitan by Nishi-Ohashi] A clean, stylish and roomy ramen shop a minute from Nishi-Ohashi Station, family friendly and open every day. The house bowl is a thick, creamy chicken paitan (¥1,000), almost potage-like, lifted with a truffle sauce and served with lemon and black pepper to change the flavor; thin whole-wheat noodles hold it well. There's also a rich shoyu, an aged salt, tsukemen and a chilled paitan in summer. In the evening, a ¥800 set of kara-age, draft beer and good menma is a bargain. Two diners found the chashu tough. Cash only.

osaka_iekei_isshinya_sakuragawa.notes: [Ramen · Yokohama iekei by the Sakuragawa crossing, open past midnight] A friendly Yokohama iekei shop on Sennichimae-dori, open until 00:30 every day, with a counter and tables. Order the tonkotsu shoyu (or shio) the iekei way, setting noodle firmness, richness and oil, on thick wavy noodles with chashu, quail eggs, spinach and nori; it's rich but not heavy. Then raid the free toppings: chopped onion, garlic, ginger, pickles and pepper. There's also a negi shio ramen and a sesame-heavy tantanmen. A rice set comes with refills, and the shop's app hands out free toppings and side-dish coupons. Cash only.

osaka_son_goku_minamisenba.notes: [Chinese · ¥800 egg rice bowls at a busy lunch counter, Minami-Senba] A popular neighborhood Chinese lunch spot near Nagahoribashi where office workers queue after noon. There's also a vegetable-packed ankake champon (season it with the table vinegar and pepper), a soy-sauce yakisoba and sara udon. Hours aren't listed; one diner notes it opens at 11:30 and closes Sundays, Mondays and holidays. Cash only.

osaka_chinese_hana_shinmachi.notes: [Chinese · big-portion budget Chinese lunches since 2006, Shinmachi] A large, unfussy Chinese restaurant on a back street near Yotsubashi, around for about twenty years and full of office workers at lunch. The listing says the cooking is by Chinese chefs trained in China. The appeal is volume for the price: a mapo tofu rice bowl set for ¥600, or a stir-fry set around ¥800 that comes with soup, a mini ramen, spring rolls and pickles. The spicy miso ramen set is properly hot; ask to adjust. Side dishes sometimes differ from the menu photos, and one diner found the taste just average. Evenings run a table-order all-you-can-eat-and-drink for ¥3,580. Cash only; smoking allowed. Closed Sundays.

The bowls are inventive: a tomato ramen made with eight tomatoes, curry and keema curry ramen, tsukemen with a choice of dip, and a properly chilled salt-lemon ramen in summer. Snack first on crisp winged gyoza, kara-age with tartar or grilled salted tomato with garlic chips. A ¥1,000 dinner set pairs keema curry ramen with a grilled-chashu bowl. Note the 20% surcharge after 10 pm. One diner found the tsukemen dip salty.

Pick a spice level from 1 to 4 at the ticket machine (2 is the standard and balances heat and numbing well), then mix the thin, firm curly noodles with the sesame sauce, meat miso and green onion thirty times before eating. Grind on extra Sichuan pepper, add cilantro if you like it heaped, and finish by putting half rice (¥100) into the leftover sauce with a splash of vinegar. A bowl is ¥800. Closed Sundays.

osaka_ron_sakuragawa.notes: [Chinese · a Beijing-style neighborhood Chinese since 1970, Sakuragawa] A busy, old-school neighborhood Chinese restaurant a minute from Sakuragawa Station, open since 1970, with plastic food samples in the window, menus on the walls, tables and tatami, and a lunchtime crowd of office workers. Food comes fast and the seasoning is lighter than typical neighborhood Chinese. Try the gomoku yakimeshi with its firm grains, the thin-noodled curry champon set, or the Chinese-style katsudon in a sweet ankake sauce; the handmade gyoza are half price on Fridays. Cash only. Closed Tuesdays.

osaka_renge_ramen_uehonmachi.notes: [Ramen · an old-timer's Kumamoto-style tonkotsu counter in Haihai Town] A nine-seat ramen counter in the basement of Uehonmachi's Haihai Town, a survivor among the arcade's izakaya and run by an elderly couple, with a gruff-but-friendly owner who has known some diners for a decade. The Renge Ramen is a gentle, natural tonkotsu in the Kumamoto line, ¥800 with a 1.5 serving of noodles free; miso is the other popular choice. The noodles are soft and high in water, so ask for firm, though one diner found even those soft. Pair it with the Sarameshi set (¥1,000), a lightly seasoned mixed rice. Lunch only except Friday nights. Cash only.

osaka_ramen_kiroku_nipponbashi.notes: [Ramen · an old-style shoyu ramen counter with ¥700 sets, Nipponbashi] A retro, long-running neighborhood ramen counter on Sakaisuji, south of Nipponbashi 4-chome, with prices from another era: shoyu ramen from ¥630, a set with a warm hand-formed rice ball for ¥700, or half fried rice for ¥800. A reviewer took the staff to be a couple. The bowl is plain and comforting, a cloudy chicken-and-pork-bone shoyu without back fat, medium-thick straight noodles, tender chashu and plenty of green onion; the fried rice is fluffy and lightly seasoned. One diner recommends it large with firm noodles. Opening can run late, so allow some slack. Cash only. Closed Mondays and Thursdays.

osaka_iekei_kouraya_nishihonmachi.notes: [Ramen · a dependable Yokohama iekei by Utsubo Park] A busy little iekei shop south of Utsubo Park, near Honmachi Station, popular with office workers at lunch. One reviewer found the owner and staff to be women; another believed the staff were from China. The ajitama ramen (¥1,000) is a rich tonkotsu shoyu on thick noodles with spinach, chashu, an egg and three big sheets of nori worth dipping; order the noodle firmness, flavor strength and oil you like, then add ginger, onion or the hot spicy miso from the table. Small rice is free before 6 pm, and there's a tea bar at lunch. Staff are polite and quick. Buy a ticket; cash only. Closed Sundays.

osaka_ajisen_ramen_senba.notes: [Ramen · a Kumamoto ramen chain branch with tai-pien, Senba] A weekday-lunch branch of the Kumamoto ramen chain Ajisen, two floors down in the Senba Center Building and connected to Sakaisuji-Honmachi Station. osaka_chuka_soba_nisei_itachibori.notes: [Ramen · a miso specialist from the Kasumi team, Awaza] An eight-seat miso ramen shop near Awaza Station, launched by the team behind nearby Ramen Kasumi. The plain miso pairs medium-thick curly noodles with a rich broth, and monthly specials rotate. The first bottle of beer is ¥100 with edamame. One longtime diner felt the miso had thinned since opening and found the service curt. Cash only. Closed Sundays.

osaka_saika_uehonmachi.notes: [Ramen · Tenri-style garlic stamina ramen, Uehonmachi] The Uehonmachi outpost of Saika, the garlicky stamina ramen from Tenri in Nara, open until midnight every day. The bowl is unmistakable: a spicy soy broth soaked with stir-fried pork belly, a heap of napa cabbage and garlic chives, and a house chili sauce, over thin curly noodles; order the noodles firm and add more garlic from the table. Unlike the chain's own shops, this one lets you double the vegetables (+¥300). Pair it with a half fried rice or gyoza with miso sauce. Quick, friendly service. osaka_ninniku_ramen_mugiyoshi_itachibori.notes: [Ramen · garlic tonkotsu shoyu, open to 00:30, Awaza] A bright, clean, roomy garlic-ramen shop on Amidaike-suji near Awaza, open until 00:30 and handy after a night out. osaka_chikappa_tanimachi4.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–14:30 and 18:00–23:00 (Tabelog). Opened 14 May 2025 (Tabelog). Cards, PayPay and Rakuten Pay accepted (Tabelog). Family friendly (Tabelog).
osaka_chikappa_tanimachi4.notes: [Ramen · Hakata tonkotsu by Tanimachi 4-chome] A cheerful Hakata-style tonkotsu shop a short walk from Tanimachi 4-chome, open lunch and late evening every day since 2025. Order the white tonkotsu with thin straight noodles barikata (extra firm): the broth is rich but finishes clean, topped with wood ear, green onion, nori and thick, tender chashu. The black version adds a pungent black-garlic oil. Then load up from the free takana and pickled ginger on the counter. Sets add half fried rice and kara-age, though one diner found the ramen bland and the kara-age greasy. Cards and PayPay accepted.

chef_bio.background: Hakata tonkotsu ramen shop (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The tonkotsu broth was rich but not overly so, with a solid depth of flavor and umami. The aftertaste was surprisingly refreshing, and it paired perfectly with the barikata thin noodles." — September 2026.
"My companion ordered the black tonkotsu ramen. The black garlic oil was prominent, and this is definitely something you should try." — August 2026.

A free side (croquette, fried shumai, kara-age or gyoza) above a set spend (2025–2026). Lines at times late at night (August 2026).
osaka_naniwa_shinpu_nipponbashi.notes: [Ramen · late-night ramen and tsukemen by Ebisucho Station] A busy, casual ramen shop right by Ebisucho Station, open until 2 am, with a long menu and a line at times late in the evening. The seafood tsukemen (¥1,100) is the standout, thick noodles in a dip heavy with bonito; the shoyu tonkotsu and a gentle sesame miso (spice to order) are both ¥980, and the abura-soba with egg yolk has its loyal fans. Spend over a set amount and a croquette, fried shumai, kara-age or gyoza comes free. A good finish to a night out. Closed Thursdays; no cards.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The dipping sauce has a rich flavor with a strong seafood essence. The umami from the bonito is prominent, and it pairs perfectly with the noodles." — August 2026, tsukemen.
"The rich yet not overwhelming flavor of the pork bone broth, combined with the sharpness of soy sauce, created a comforting deliciousness…" — July 2026, Shoyu Tonkotsu ¥980.

osaka_menya_aozora_tsutenkaku.notes: [Ramen · Hakata tonkotsu near Tsutenkaku] A calm tonkotsu shop a block from Tsutenkaku, recently moved here from Sennichimae-dori, with multilingual QR ordering and every kind of payment. The Hakata Yatai Tonkotsu (¥900) is a foamy, well-balanced bowl on thin noodles that even a tonkotsu-shy diner enjoyed; the house original, Shin Nara Tonkotsu (¥900), crosses it with Nara stamina ramen, red with chili at the spicy setting and topped with extra pork. Sets add kara-age and fried rice, though one diner found the rice pre-made. Open 11:00–23:00 daily.

chef_bio.origin: Sister shop of the Nipponbashi branch; moved here from Sennichimae-dori (April and August 2026 reviews).

"I ordered… [the] original 'Shin Nara Tonkotsu Ramen' for JPY 900. It's said to combine the best of Hakata tonkotsu and Nara stamina ramen." — April 2026.

osaka_ramen_cho_hiranomachi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; soy-based broth.
osaka_ramen_cho_hiranomachi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:00–23:00; closed Sun and public holidays (Tabelog). Cash only (Tabelog). Garlic added only if you want it (2026).
osaka_ramen_cho_hiranomachi.notes: [Ramen · a light, cheap garlic ramen in the office district, Hiranomachi] A simple ramen shop behind a clear vinyl entrance and a bright yellow "garlic ramen" sign near Kitahama, with a tiny ground-floor counter and tables upstairs. The ramen (¥750) is light and old-fashioned, with flavorful soy-seasoned chashu; the owner asks whether you want garlic, which hides as whole cloves at the bottom of the bowl. Two diners found the garlic milder and the broth plainer than the sign promises, but it is cheap and easy after a night out. A ramen set with rice is ¥900. Cash only. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Neighborhood ramen shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "When you order ramen here, the owner kindly asks, 'Would you like garlic with that?'… The ramen at this restaurant is very light." — May 2026, ramen ¥750.

"The flavor was light… Hidden at the bottom were some garlic cloves, which added a nice punch when eaten. The chashu was well-seasoned with soy sauce, giving it a nostalgic taste." — July 2026, Ramen Set Meal ¥900.

osaka_naniwa_gomi_hatchin_ramen_shinseka.notes: [Ramen · late-night stamina ramen and curry under Tsutenkaku] A small ramen shop at the foot of Tsutenkaku, open from 10 am until 4 am every day, that also serves Kanazawa-style Go Go Curry. The negi ramen (¥1,150) is a Tenri-style stamina bowl: a soy broth full of napa cabbage with a kick of chili and garlic, thin curly noodles and a heap of green onion; add a fluffy half fried rice for ¥300. The thick pork-cutlet curry, eaten with a fork, is the alternative. Tables at the back feel tucked away. One diner found the service inattentive. Every payment type accepted.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop that also serves Go Go Curry (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The soy sauce-based broth, packed with vegetables mainly consisting of napa cabbage, has a delightful kick of spiciness and a punch of garlic, reminiscent of the flavors found in Tenri ramen." — August 2026, Large Negi Ramen ¥1,300.

osaka_satsuma_ramen_uehonmachi.notes: [Ramen · a lunch-only old-school tonkotsu shop with a ¥500 student bowl, Uehonmachi] A long-running neighborhood ramen shop in a residential street south of Uehonmachi, open only 11:00–14:00 and busy with students from the nearby high school, who get a ¥500 ramen. The bowl is a light, nostalgic tonkotsu with soft medium-thick noodles and a tender slice of chashu; one diner found it too mild. The sets are the value: ramen with half fried rice for about ¥950, or the slightly spicy curry fried rice set (¥1,000); dip the plain fried rice in the soup. Bright red kimchi comes with the set meal. Cash only.

osaka_kairikiya_aeon_dome_city.hours_raw: Daily 10:00–21:00 (Tabelog). Opened 11 December 2020 (Tabelog). Cards and e-money accepted; no QR (Tabelog). Food-court seating; kids menu (Tabelog). App coupons, e.g. half-price fried rice (September 2026).
osaka_kairikiya_aeon_dome_city.notes: [Ramen · Kyoto back-fat shoyu in a food court by Kyocera Dome] A branch of the Kyoto Kitashirakawa ramen chain Kairikiya, in the fourth-floor food court of AEON Mall by Kyocera Dome, handy before a ballgame and good for families. The house bowl is Kyoto shoyu ramen under a layer of pork back fat that eats lighter than it looks, slightly sweet, on thin straight noodles with chashu and green onion; the seasoned-egg version is ¥1,001. Sets add fragrant fried rice and crisp kara-age. Food comes in minutes. One diner found the soup lukewarm. Open 10:00–21:00 daily.

chef_bio.origin: Branch of Kairikiya, a ramen chain that began in Kitashirakawa, Kyoto (September 2026 review).

osaka_wa_dining_seino_spaworld.notes: [Ramen · Wakayama ramen inside Spa World, Shinsekai] The Spa World branch of Seino, a well-known Wakayama ramen shop, in the third-floor food zone of the Shinsekai bathhouse, so you need to be inside the spa to eat here, and you settle up by barcode as you leave. The classic Seino Wakayama ramen is a rich pork-bone shoyu with a strong soy edge, thin straight noodles and rare chashu; there's also a light Hokkaido-style shio, a summer chilled ume-and-shiso ramen and a winter oyster black ramen. One diner paired it with a beer after the bath; another finds the Wakayama original better. Open 11:00–23:00.

chef_bio.origin: Spa World branch of Seino, a Wakayama ramen shop (2026 reviews); opened 1 July 2023 (Tabelog).

osaka_ramen_man_hiranomachi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; shoyu tare; gyoza.
osaka_ramen_man_hiranomachi.hours_raw: No hours on Tabelog; a March 2026 review confirms it open. Cash only (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (Tabelog). Run by one person (December 2024).
osaka_ramen_man_hiranomachi.notes: [Ramen · a one-person spicy chashu ramen counter, Kitahama] An old-fashioned ramen counter near Kitahama, run single-handed. The house Ramen Man is a pork-bone shoyu heaped with sliced and coarse-ground chili, bean sprouts and green onion, with chopped garlic if you want it; the chili isn't powdered into the soup, so the heat doesn't swamp the broth. The chashu ramen packs eight or nine small, tender pork-belly slices, and order it at spice level 2 or 3. Sets with rice and kimchi run ¥800–1,000. Smoking is allowed, which surprised one diner. Hours aren't listed. Cash only.

osaka_teppan_kobo_panyo_dotonbori.notes: [Teppanyaki · a 12-seat Dotonbori teppan counter with a river-view room] A small teppanyaki restaurant at street level on Dotonbori: seven counter seats facing the griddle and a semi-private room at the back that looks out on the Dotonbori River. The house course, the Panyo Dinner, runs through seared meat sushi, a Panyo burger and a domestic tenderloin; steaks can be upgraded to Special Wagyu or Matsusaka beef, and shrimp and abalone come live from the tank. A December 2025 course had grilled turnip, pumpkin and green onion and an 80 g tenderloin with salt, garlic and wasabi, then garlic rice with a light chicken soup. Diners have booked lunch courses for celebrations; on request the kitchen cooked the meat sushi through, and a birthday dessert came with fireworks in place of candles and a message. Dinner about ¥8,000–10,000, lunch ¥3,000–4,000 (Tabelog).

osaka_fujun_kissa_artemis_souemoncho.notes: [Café · a Showa-retro night kissa open until 6 am, Souemoncho] A second-floor night café off Souemoncho, done up in Showa-retro style, that opens at 19:00 on weekdays (13:00 at weekends) and runs until 6 am. osaka_gekko_teppan_higashishinsaibashi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: the signature Gekko-yaki and okonomiyaki use a batter, the yakisoba is wheat noodles, and sauces are not described. Grilled seafood with salt and grilled asparagus are on the menu; ask about the shared teppan.

osaka_gekko_teppan_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Teppanyaki · a 10-seat round-counter teppan with its own Gekko-yaki, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, grown-up teppanyaki bar in a corner of a Higashi-Shinsaibashi building, with six seats around the griddle and one table, where the owner cooks in front of you and pours from a short list of red wines. The signature is Gekko-yaki, a fluffy egg-and-cabbage cake with thick pork, and two diners single out the kimchi-cheese version (¥2,700); the seafood yakisoba carbonara (¥2,500) folds shrimp and scallops into thick chewy noodles under a soft egg. Simpler plates: shrimp, squid and scallops grilled with salt, cabbage stir-fried with abura-kasu, grilled asparagus, salty grilled beef intestine. One diner found the seasoning salty overall. Expect about ¥6,000–8,000. Students may be turned away, children by arrangement only, and there's a dress code (no sandals or sweats).

osaka_korean_komone_sennichimae.notes: [Korean · a two-person basement Korean spot for soy-marinated crab, Sennichimae] A 16-seat basement Korean restaurant off Sennichimae, run by a friendly couple aged 70-something, open from 16:00 to 2 am and busy late; one night it was nearly full at 23:30. Come for the house-made ganjang gejang, crab marinated in soy (¥2,700 small, ¥5,500 large), or the sweet-spicy yangnyeom version, served with gloves; the soy-marinated shrimp is the other draw. Also cheese jeon, tender steamed pork, samgyetang, and an octopus, offal and shrimp hot pot for two that needs booking. Makgeolli comes by the bottle or ladled from a big bowl, and there's bottle keep. One diner found the food average and a little pricey but the service warm; another said it felt like coming home. English and Korean menus (Tabelog). Closed Wednesdays.

Two diners praise the plating, one the chef's funny conversation; another found the course price on the high side. About ¥8,000–15,000; ¥550 service charge.

osaka_wabekari_pandoraya_nishishinsaibas.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a bakery of buns, croissants and Danish pastries; no gluten-free items described.
osaka_wabekari_pandoraya_nishishinsaibas.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: custard and cream fillings, a quail-egg yakisoba bun and a chicken sandwich; nothing described as vegan.
osaka_wabekari_pandoraya_nishishinsaibas.hours_raw: Tue–Sun and holidays 10:00–20:00; closed Monday and the day after a holiday (Tabelog). Two reviews (August 2025, May 2026) give 10:00–20:00 daily, so check Mondays. Opened 18 September 2024 (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). Bakery on 1F, eat-in on 2F with outlets and Wi-Fi (May 2026); claim a seat upstairs before ordering (August 2026).
osaka_wabekari_pandoraya_nishishinsaibas.notes: [Bakery café · puppy-shaped buns and Japanese tea, Amerikamura] A small bakery in Amerikamura whose idea is bread that goes with Japanese tea: buy downstairs, then eat upstairs in a calm, Japanese-style room with cushions, outlets and Wi-Fi. The star is the puppy bun (¥330), custard in the head and chocolate or hojicha cream in the body, with a Shiba Inu version (weekends only, per one diner) and a pink one that one diner took to hold strawberry jam. Also a dango Danish (¥300), a mitarashi dango bun, a clover-shaped Kyoto matcha anpan, a melon bread with a face and a yakisoba bun under a fried quail egg. There's a tea of the day to taste, and Japanese tea ordered with bread is ¥200 off. Buns are small and cheap, so it's easy to try two or three. Claim a seat upstairs before ordering.

chef_bio.background: Bakery with an eat-in floor (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Bread that pairs with Japanese tea (May–June 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The concept of this bakery is 'bread that pairs well with Japanese tea.' [There is] a tasting of the tea of the day, and if you order a set with tea, you can enjoy a discount of JPY 200 on your drink." — June 2026.
"The head is filled with custard, while the body has chocolate cream, allowing you to enjoy two different flavors." — May 2026, Puppy Bread ¥330.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 和ベーカリーぱんどら屋、大阪市中央区西心斎橋2-9-37、大阪難波駅から419m、火〜日・祝10:00〜20:00、月曜と祝日の翌日休み、2024年9月18日開店、カード・電子マネー・QR可、15席。口コミ(2025年8月〜2026年9月): アメリカ村のパン屋、日本茶に合うパンがコンセプト、本日のお茶の試飲、パンと一緒に日本茶を頼むと200円引き、1階がパン売り場で2階がイートイン (和の雰囲気、クッション、電源、Wi-Fi)、子犬のパン330円 (頭はカスタード、体はチョコか hojicha)、週末だけの柴犬のパン330円、いちごジャム入りらしいピンクの子犬、dango のデニッシュ300円、mitarashi dango のパン、塩クロワッサン、いちごのクロワッサン、抹茶のクロワッサン、抹茶のデニッシュ、顔のあるメロンパン、3色の Pandora メロンパン、四つ葉の形の京都抹茶 anpan、うずらの目玉焼きをのせた yakisoba のパン、ハニーマスタードチキンのサンド490円、ピーチティー、2階は先に席を取ってから注文を。

osaka_buttocks_venison_sennichimae.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; venison roast and carpaccio are on the menu, alongside a breaded cutlet, fried gyoza, mazesoba and garlic toast.
osaka_buttocks_venison_sennichimae.hours_raw: Mon–Sat and holidays 11:00–14:00 and 18:00–04:00; Sunday 18:00–04:00; food last order 03:00, drinks 04:00; open year-round (Tabelog). Dinner appetizer/service charge ¥500 (Tabelog). The second floor can be booked as a private room for 5 or more (Tabelog). Children welcome (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). Designated smoking area (Tabelog).
osaka_buttocks_venison_sennichimae.notes: [Venison · a deer-meat izakaya open to 4 am, Sennichimae] A small venison specialist on the Aioibashi-suji shopping street, nearly everything on the menu made from deer, and open for lunch and then from 18:00 to 4 am. The master's second son also works in the room. Several diners say the meat is lean, tender and free of gamey smell. The ¥2,500 lunch course brings a freshly fried venison cutlet, a low-temperature roast and venison fried rice; at night try the venison carpaccio, a juicy roast with salt and fried onions, rillettes on baguette, and the deer bread, roast venison on salty garlic toast. Newer dishes include crisp pleatless venison gyoza and a peppery venison mazesoba with egg yolk. A seven-dish venison yaki-shabu course (¥7,500) needs booking; one diner wished the cuts were explained. One diner noted a generous wine pour. ¥500 dinner charge.

chef_bio.background: Venison izakaya and bar (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews). The master's second son also works in the room (April 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Venison cutlet; roast venison; deer bread.

anecdotes.text: "The venison is lean, with no fat… The freshly fried cutlet has a rich flavor, yet no gamey taste at all, and it's incredibly tender and delicious!" — May 2026, Venison Feast Lunch Course ¥2,500.
"The carpaccio had no gamey taste at all, and I felt the meatiness was even stronger than beef. The roast was perfectly cooked and juicy…" — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 鹿肉料理専門店 バトックス、大阪市中央区千日前1-4-19 中島ビル 1F、相合橋筋商店街、なんば駅から徒歩5分、月〜土・祝11:00〜14:00、18:00〜翌4:00、日18:00〜翌4:00 (料理L.O. 3:00、ドリンクL.O. 4:00)、年中無休、ディナーはお通し・サービス料500円、20席、2階は5人から貸切の個室、子ども連れ歓迎、カード・電子マネー・QR可、分煙。口コミ(2025年11月〜2026年10月): 鹿肉の専門店、臭みがなくやわらかいという声が複数、鹿肉のランチコース2,500円 (鹿カツ、低温調理のロースト、鹿肉のチャーハン)、鹿パン (ガーリックトーストにローストした鹿肉)、鹿肉のリエット、リエットのポテトサラダ、カルパッチョ、塩とフライドオニオンとソースで食べるロースト、ひだのない揚げた鹿肉の gyoza、辛さを選べる鹿肉の mazesoba、カルボナーラ、要予約の鹿肉の yaki-shabu のコース7品7,500円、部位の説明がなかったという声、ワインをたっぷり注いでくれたという声。

osaka_512_cafe_sweets_shinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the pancake batter is made with eggs (September 2026), served with cream and ice cream.
osaka_512_cafe_sweets_shinsaibashi.hours_raw: Daily 9:00–17:00, open year-round (Tabelog); a September 2026 review gives 10:00–17:00, last order 16:00. Reservations taken. Cards, e-money and PayPay accepted (Tabelog). Order by QR code on your phone; water is self-service (June 2026). Non-smoking. Children welcome; takeout (Tabelog). Opened 16 July 2020 (Tabelog).
osaka_512_cafe_sweets_shinsaibashi.notes: [Café · jiggly pancakes up a staircase, Shinsaibashi-suji] A second-floor pancake café off Shinsaibashi-suji, reached by a staircase straight from the door. The pancakes are the tall, wobbling kind, so soft one diner said they eat like a drink: the standard has a crisp caramelized top with custard inside, whipped cream, vanilla ice cream and berry sauce, plus a bitter caramel to adjust the sweetness. Seasonal versions include matcha with matcha custard and mascarpone (¥1,800 + tax), peach and mascarpone, and a summer chocolate-mint. For lunch there's a plate of French toast with bacon and eggs. Pancakes came in about 10 minutes for one diner. One weekday afternoon was quiet; one holiday lunch the two-person tables were nearly full. Order by QR code.

chef_bio.background: Pancake café (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal, natural ingredients (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "The freshly made pancakes were incredibly fluffy—so soft that they felt like a drink rather than food… The caramelized surface was crispy, and when I cut into it, I could see a hint of custard sauce inside." — June 2026.
"The lunch plate included French toast, bacon and eggs, chips, salad, and canelé. (The contents may change occasionally.)" — August 2026, 512 Lunch Plate.

osaka_nonoya_sennichimae.notes: [Chicken · grill-your-own Tajima chicken over charcoal, Sennichimae] A small chicken specialist a few minutes from Nippombashi where you grill fresh Tajima chicken yourself, yakiniku style, on a charcoal brazier set in front of you. Order neck, thigh, skin, chewy older-hen meat or rarer heart cuts, then fill in with the raw dishes several diners single out: a chicken sashimi platter, liver sashimi and chicken sashimi with tororo. The chicken nanban and salt-stir-fried liver are thick but tender, and there are chicken hot pots and shabu-shabu for groups. The counter at the front lets you talk with the staff; the raised room at the back can be fully booked. It gets smoky, so dress for it. Opens 18:00, closed Mondays; AMEX is the only card.

chef_bio.background: Chicken izakaya with table grills (Tabelog; 2023–2025 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Tajima chicken sourced fresh (Tabelog listing; May 2025).

anecdotes.text: "Yakitori is served on skewers, but the grilled chicken here is prepared in a yakiniku style… However, it does produce a lot of smoke." — June 2024.
"The Chicken Sashimi is so rich and silky! Both the Chicken Nanban and the liver stir-fry are thick but incredibly tender." — December 2024.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: のの屋、大阪市中央区千日前1-6-6、日本橋駅から徒歩3分、火〜日18:00〜24:00、月曜定休、2019年6月5日開店、予約可、席料250円、カードはAMEXのみ、電子マネー・QR不可、喫煙可、16席 (カウンター8、座敷の個室8)、但馬の鶏を炭火で焼く鶏の焼肉、鍋やコースも。口コミ(2023年12月〜2025年5月): 卓上で自分で焼く、首、もも、皮、親鶏、kokoro no kori という心臓の部位、鶏の sashimi の盛り合わせ、レバーの sashimi、tororo をかけた鶏の sashimi、もも肉の tataki、chicken nanban、レバーの塩炒め、鶏の天ぷら、ねぎのサラダ、鶏とポテトのチーズ、鶏鍋と鶏の shabu-shabu、もやしの namul、卵焼き、カウンターでは店の人と話せる、奥の座敷は予約で埋まる、煙が多いので服に注意、入口がふたつ。

osaka_antica_osteria_dal_spello_namba.notes: [Italian · a 10-seat Namba osteria with handmade pasta, cash only] A tiny Italian restaurant a few minutes from Namba Station, black and wood inside, with four counter seats and two tables, sister to SPELLO in Sakaisuji-Honmachi. The chewy handmade pasta comes up in several reviews: oyster and bottarga pasta with three big oysters, oyster pasta in January. Lunch is ¥1,800, a reserved lunch course ¥2,500, and a fuller ¥4,800 course with a drink runs from crab appetizers and onion-corn soup with fresh onion focaccia to sea bream and coconut tiramisu. Over 30 Italian wines, with pairing suggestions. One cook runs the kitchen, so dishes come at a leisurely pace; tables are close. One diner rated the cooking average but the value excellent. Cash only; closed Tuesdays and the 1st and 3rd Wednesdays.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 9 June 2018 (Tabelog); sister restaurant of SPELLO in Sakaisuji-Honmachi (January 2026 review).
chef_bio.background: Small Italian osteria with one cook in the kitchen (2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "…the classic homemade pasta, known for its chewy texture, paired excellently with the sauce… With over 30 varieties of Italian wines available, the staff also suggested options that complemented our dishes…" — January 2026, dinner.
"The pasta with oysters and bottarga had three large oysters and was pleasantly spicy and delicious." — May 2026, lunch with one drink ¥4,800.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: アンティカ オステリア ダル スペッロ、大阪市中央区難波4-7-5 光栄ビル 1F、なんば駅13番出口から徒歩3分、月・水・金〜日・祝11:30〜15:00 (料理L.O. 14:30)、18:00〜22:30 (料理L.O. 21:30)、木12:00〜14:00、火曜と第1・第3水曜休み、2018年6月9日開店、予約可、現金のみ、サービス料・チャージなし、禁煙、10席 (カウンター4、テーブル2)、ワインにこだわり、公式サイトあり。口コミ(2026年1〜7月): 堺筋本町の SPELLO の姉妹店、もちもちの手打ちパスタ、カルパッチョ、海鮮と季節の野菜、肉料理、イタリアワイン30種以上、ランチ1,800円、要予約のランチコース2,500円、ドリンクつき4,800円 (蟹の入った前菜、玉ねぎとコーンのスープ、玉ねぎのフォカッチャ、牡蠣と bottarga のパスタ、鯛のポワレ、ココナッツのティラミス)、聖護院かぶのスープ、牡蠣のパスタ、ローストチキン、厨房はひとりで提供はゆっくり、席の間は狭め、コスパはいいが味は普通という声。

osaka_showa_futago_yaki_higashishinsaiba.notes: [Korean · an 8-seat Showa-retro Korean bar for gimbap and sundae, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A street-level Korean bar in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, run by two people and styled like a 1970s–80s Showa izakaya crossed with a Korean street stall, open until 2 am. The shop is run by Korean twins. Gimbap is the draw, in many varieties; one diner ordered a half roll and got a whole one. One diner calls it a rare find for sundae, Korean blood sausage; there's also bulgogi, jeon and Korean oden that one diner calls a must with Korean beer or Chamisul. One diner found prices well above Korea's. Eight seats around the counter, friendly service, smoking allowed and pets welcome; leftovers can go home with you. English and Korean menus (Tabelog). Opens 19:00 on weekdays, 17:00 at weekends.

chef_bio.background: Korean bar run by two people (November 2024 review; Tabelog). The shop is run by Korean twins (November 2024 review).

anecdotes.text: "It's rare to find a place in Japan that serves sundae… In fact, the gimbap is the main attraction here! There are many different types of gimbap available!" — August 2024.
"The Korean oden is absolutely delicious, so I highly recommend trying it when you go! It pairs perfectly with Korean beer and Chamisul as well." — February 2025.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 昭和双子焼き (旧店名 双子のり巻き)、大阪市中央区東心斎橋2-6-1、長堀橋駅・心斎橋駅から徒歩10分、月〜金19:00〜翌2:00、土日祝17:00〜翌2:00 (L.O. 1:30)、年中無休、お通し250円、カード可、電子マネー・QR不可、喫煙可、8席 (カウンター、立ち飲み)、ペット可、テイクアウト、英語・韓国語のメニュー、写真つきメニュー、昭和の居酒屋の雰囲気で oden、串、韓国料理、日本酒、ウイスキー。口コミ(2024年6月〜2026年8月): 韓国の屋台のような雰囲気、gimbap がいちばんの目当てで種類が多い、半分を頼んだら1本出てきた、sundae の盛り合わせ、bulgogi、jeon、韓国の oden、韓国のビールと Chamisul、残りは持ち帰れる、韓国より値段はかなり高いという声、スタッフが親しみやすい。

Cards, iD/QUICPay and PayPay accepted (Tabelog). Heated tobacco only, dinner only (Tabelog). Opened 15 November 2025; formerly Wabisuke, same owner (Tabelog; August 2026).
osaka_sakaba_neiro_shinsaibashi.notes: [Izakaya · a 10-seat back-alley counter with set-meal lunches, Shinsaibashi] A quiet 10-seat counter in an alley just off the busy Shinsaibashi-suji arcade, reopened in November 2025 under a new name by the owner of the former Wabisuke, with an Okinawan streak. Lunch is a tray set: pick a main such as the gently seasoned meat tofu (¥1,100) or chicken nanban with both mentaiko and tartar sauce, with rice refills, miso soup, small sides and a raw egg for egg-over-rice. At night order the obanzai assortment (¥990), which one diner saw every table order, plus rafute tacos (¥550) with hot sauce, tako-wasa with nagaimo, crab gratin and shrimp gyoza. Lunch can be reserved, which helps with so few seats.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 15 November 2025 (Tabelog); formerly Wabisuke, same owner (August 2026 review).

Opened 30 September 2023 (Tabelog).
osaka_ten_carat_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Tempura · a 13-seat late-night tempura counter with creative pieces, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, stylish tempura counter in Higashi-Shinsaibashi that stays open until 3 am. The ¥4,400 course is the easy way in: a toro-taku canapé on seaweed tempura, a soft-boiled egg with shiba-zuke tartar, Camembert drizzled with honey, then jumbo shrimp, a whole anago and fan-cut eggplant, all served piping hot, plus the Carat Roll of salmon and sea bream wrapped with myoga and shiso. Two diners say the beef niku-sui soup, with 100% buckwheat soba to dip, stole the show; dessert is sweet-potato tempura with vanilla ice cream. Menus in English, Chinese and Korean, and English-speaking staff (Tabelog). ¥330 seat charge.

osaka_sake_bar_shiki_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Sake bar · a 10-seat Tohoku sake counter with seasonal fish, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm second-floor sake bar of ten counter seats in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open since 2015 and focused on local sake from Tohoku. Tell the staff what you like and a few get poured to try; one diner did a flight of one brewery's range, another paired sake with bonito. The food beats bar snacks: fish bought daily, red shrimp marinated in sake (two diners single it out), Senshu water eggplant as sashimi, squid tentacles with liver mayo, Wagyu sukiyaki-style, even Okinawa soba with squid-ink yakisoba. A sashimi platter from ¥1,500 a head can be ordered a day ahead. Beginners are welcome (Tabelog). Last entry 23:00; closed Sundays and holidays; ¥300 charge.

chef_bio.background: Sake bar with seasonal fish (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal fish bought daily; local sake from Tohoku (Tabelog listing).

osaka_omusubiya_taritari_souemoncho.notes: [Izakaya · rice balls and owner-caught fish until 7 am, Souemoncho] A small izakaya in Souemoncho that pairs rice balls with fish the owner catches each week off Wakayama and Maizuru, and stays open until 7 am on most nights, handy after the last train. Start with a sashimi platter (thick-cut, from the week's catch) or a seafood rice bowl, add an extra-large fried horse mackerel that one diner calls a must, a grilled yellowtail collar or marinated mackerel, then finish with rice balls made from Niigata and Hiroshima rice and the miso soup of the day. Individual hot pots run to the 06:00 food last order. Friendly staff, counter and table seats, and children are welcome. Closed Thursdays (Tabelog).

osaka_teppanyaki_gin_hikari_higashishins.notes: [Teppanyaki · kaiseki-style teppan courses in a hotel, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, chic teppanyaki room on the second floor of a Higashi-Shinsaibashi hotel, with eight counter seats facing the griddle. The chef has more than 40 years in Japanese cuisine. The courses read like kaiseki first: five seasonal appetizers (one diner loved the fugu-skin jelly), three kinds of sashimi, a simmered dish or soup, flounder meunière cooked on the teppan, then Wagyu steak flamed in front of you, eaten with wasabi and rock salt. Garlic fried rice and miso soup close it out before fruit or a parfait. A diner noted that courses now start at ¥6,600, lower than before; two diners chose the ¥8,800 omakase. Dinner only for now, 10% service charge; closed Thursdays.

osaka_seidako_nishishinsaibashi.notes: [Takoyaki · a cash-only takoyaki izakaya open from noon to the small hours, Amerikamura] A small takoyaki bar in Amerikamura, open from noon until 2 am (3 am at weekends), as good for a daytime drink as a late one. The takoyaki has a dashi-rich batter, crisp outside and creamy within; it's good plain, but salt mayo is the topping diners keep naming, with salt butter and sauce mayo as alternatives. There's a wide snack menu for drinking, a Masachan highball, and bags of the shop's takoyaki flour to take home when they're not sold out. Cheerful staff and a sticker-covered, hidden-away feel. Cash only; smoking allowed.

osaka_takotako_king_honten_nishi.notes: [Takoyaki · late-night takoyaki and table teppan, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A branch of the TAKOTAKO KING takoyaki group, just west of the main shop, open from 18:00 to 3 am and still busy around 1 am. Upstairs, each table has its own teppan for reheating and grilling, with a toy train running past and an octopus-shaped smoke machine. Salt garlic takoyaki is the flavor diners keep naming, and a few prefer the hot, crunchy fried takoyaki; a four-flavor sampler lets you try several. Beyond takoyaki: a cheesy tororo-yaki, yam and seafood specials, grilled squid tentacles, extra-large kara-age and even omurice. Staff are usually cheerful, though one October 2026 diner found a new hire couldn't get the table grill hot. Takeout available.

osaka_39_chicken_nipponbashi.notes: [Korean fried chicken · a takeout-first Korean chicken counter, Nippombashi] The original shop of 39 Chicken, a small Korean fried-chicken counter on a shopping street near Nippombashi, open noon to 2 am and built mostly for takeout. Chicken is fried to order, bone-in or boneless, with a crunchy coating; get it plain-crispy, yangnyeom (sweet-spicy) or soy, or half-and-half (¥1,950 in November 2025), with pickled radish on the side. A medium is plenty for two. Cheese balls, tteok-and-sausage skewers and a Korean steamed egg in a stone pot round it out. One diner found the price a bit high for takeout. Few recent reviews, so check before going.

osaka_sushi_ginza_onodera_musuko_namba.notes: [Sushi · Onodera-group Edomae sushi by the piece, ordered on a tablet, Namba] A casual counter from the Ginza Onodera sushi group, on the ground floor of the Namba Oriental Hotel, where you order authentic Edomae sushi one piece at a time on a tablet, choosing size, rice amount and wasabi, and help yourself to tea like at a conveyor-belt shop. The rice is seasoned with red vinegar and the pieces arrive already brushed, so there's no soy sauce on the counter. Diners single out isaki, anago, hairy crab, akagai and the nara-zuke toro-taku hand roll; one found the featured tuna underwhelming. Shop originals include a Sennichimae Roll and 'Namba Mountain'. Expect ¥5,000–10,000; families welcome; menus in English, Chinese and Korean.
