osaka_mahoroba_irori_shinsaibashi.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; the courses use sauces (including XO sauce on the Wagyu and an abalone sauce), though one diner had a sauce changed on request (August 2026).
osaka_mahoroba_irori_shinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: courses built on seafood, Wagyu, wild boar and duck.
osaka_mahoroba_irori_shinsaibashi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat and holidays 18:00–24:00 (food last order 23:00); closed Sunday (Tabelog). Appetizer charge ¥1,000 (Tabelog). À la carte items vary with the season (Tabelog). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Heated tobacco only (Tabelog).
osaka_mahoroba_irori_shinsaibashi.notes: [Charcoal grill · seasonal irori courses over binchotan, Shinsaibashi] A calm, upscale charcoal-grill restaurant in a Shinsaibashi back alley, built around sunken irori hearths burning Kishu binchotan, which keeps smoke down. The seasonal courses run through small fish, juicy large clams, live lobster and abalone, Wagyu, wild boar, duck and vegetables, mostly grilled in front of you (one diner grilled at the hearth themselves). The Wagyu is seared with XO sauce for a smoky edge, and a thick-cut Wagyu strip-loin rice bowl is the closer two diners rave about. One diner asked to skip a sauce ingredient and the chef made an abalone-liver sauce on the spot. Expect ¥20,000–30,000 for a full course; ¥1,000 appetizer charge. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Charcoal irori restaurant (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal ingredients grilled over Kishu binchotan (August 2026 reviews).

osaka_kozara_kitchen_cocoro_higashishins.notes: [Izakaya · a cheap small-plates bar with lunch sets and smoking seats, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A cozy, stylish little izakaya near Shinsaibashi Station, marked by a red lantern, that serves cheap small plates at night (chicken liver pâté and house oil sardines from ¥350, fresh oysters in winter) and about six lunch sets by day. At lunch, try the millefeuille beef cutlet with grated daikon and ponzu (¥1,200), moo shu pork (¥900) or a light chicken-breast kara-age set (¥800); large rice is free and an iced coffee is ¥100 more. There's even a chicken-shoyu ramen on the night menu. Every seat allows smoking, which one diner came looking for. Closed Mondays.

osaka_tachinomi_cook_osso_osseyo.notes: [Standing bar · a Korean-Italian standing bar in Jumbo Yokocho, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A tiny standing bar in the Jumbo Yokocho alley of small bars off Yahata-machi street, open since 2010 and, per the listing, only three nights a week. The cooking leans Korean and properly spicy: generous, well-fermented baechu kimchi (¥350), fiery stir-fried baby octopus (¥780), shrimp jeon, and an extra-hot octopus stir-fry that one diner had made with shirako when octopus was out. Fresh oysters come with three sauces, including a gochujang one, and fruit cocktails are made to order, like a makgeolli cocktail packed with crushed strawberries. Friendly and easy for solo drinkers; one diner found prices a little high for a standing bar. Food notes are mostly from 2023; latest visit July 2025.

osaka_shabu_cho_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Hot pot · individual sukiyaki pots at a 1978 counter with lunch lines, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A Higashi-Shinsaibashi counter that has served sukiyaki and shabu-shabu since 1978, one pot per guest, and famous for its lunch line. Lunch sukiyaki starts around ¥1,400 (¥2,000 with 1.5× meat): thin-sliced marbled beef to add to a pot of udon, shirataki and vegetables in a rich, slightly sweet sauce, with egg for dipping, rice and oolong tea refilled free. Staff manage the heat if you like. Dinner moves to A5 Wagyu and pork courses, with house ponzu or sesame sauce for shabu-shabu and a signature frozen sake. When it's full you may be seated at the annex nearby. One diner suggests the less fatty cuts. Closed Sundays.

osaka_minato_kappo_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Kappo · a 1999 Osaka kappo known for its dashi, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm 15-seat kappo in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open since 1999 and proud of its dashi, with four courses and about 70 à la carte dishes on Rosanjin-style tableware. Long-time diners return for the Kumamoto horse sashimi, steamed abalone with liver, grilled sesame tofu, crab with crab miso and fried snapper scales, and one now always finishes with the sea bream chazuke in rich sesame sauce. Prices aren't shown on the à la carte list: one diner paid just over ¥16,000; ¥10,000–15,000 is typical. Over a dozen sakes. It asks for quiet: no sandals or shorts, no strong fragrance, and no children below school age.

osaka_opera_namba_spanish.hours_raw: Daily 17:30–23:30; irregular closures (Tabelog). Seat charge ¥300 (Tabelog). Two-hour seating; no children of middle-school age or younger; no birthday plates; all guests should arrive together (Tabelog). Cards and PayPay accepted; no e-money (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). osaka_opera_namba_spanish.notes: [Spanish · a pintxos counter with Japanese twists, Namba] A small Spanish bar on a side street near Namba Station, the Namba branch of an OPERA in Honmachi, opened October 2025. The pintxos sit in a row at the counter like a sushi display, each on French bread with its own sauce: shiitake, shrimp and zucchini, vongole, sardine with tomato, shirasu and avocado. Order the seasonal seafood paella and the grilled octopus early, since they take time. Thirteen wines by the glass. It's often full and service can be slow; one diner saw a single person running it. Two-hour limit, ¥300 seat charge, no children.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 8 October 2025; a second shop after OPERA in Honmachi (Tabelog; August 2026 review).
chef_bio.background: Spanish pintxos bar with a staff-maintained Tabelog listing (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Spanish dishes with seasonal Japanese ingredients (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "Right in front of the counter seats is the pinchos counter, reminiscent of a sushi bar… Even the French bread at the bottom was tasty." — August 2026.
"Since the main dishes and paella take some time to prepare, we ordered those right away… Since it was a one-person operation, we took our time sipping wine while we waited." — August 2026.

Smoking at every seat (Tabelog). Cards and QR accepted; no e-money (Tabelog). No voicemail reservations (Tabelog). Opened 4 April 2014 (Tabelog).
osaka_shun_sai_ka_naka_higashishinsaibas.notes: [Chinese · a basement creative-Chinese counter open to 2 am, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A cozy basement Chinese restaurant in Higashi-Shinsaibashi with six counter seats and sunken kotatsu tables, open until 2 am most nights. The menu changes daily and leans seasonal and vegetable-rich, with diners comparing it to hotel Chinese at izakaya prices: roast char siu (¥1,100), cuttlefish in Hong Kong sauce (¥1,400), plump spicy stir-fried oysters (¥1,500), sweet-and-sour spare ribs, braised beef, clams with thick glass noodles, and soup noodles two diners single out. Ask and the kitchen will make fried rice or ramen off the menu. Portions suit sharing among two or three. Smoking at every seat. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Creative Chinese restaurant (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Daily-changing menu with seasonal ingredients (October–November 2025 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "This restaurant offers hotel-quality Chinese food at izakaya prices… the beef tataki and the soup noodles were especially outstanding!!!" — 2025–2026 review.
"…if you ask, they will even make fried rice or ramen that isn't listed… I highly recommend the sweet and sour spare ribs, kara-age chicken neck, and green pepper beef stir-fry…" — August 2026.

cultural_comfort.note: Small counter; smoking at every seat (Tabelog).

Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Heated tobacco only (Tabelog). All-you-can-drink available (Tabelog). Opened 9 April 2018 (Tabelog).
osaka_kakure_toriuo_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Japanese · a signless, reservation-only small-plates course in private rooms, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A deliberately hidden Japanese restaurant with no sign on the street: look for a small red sign on the Yahata-suji side of the Nippo Jumbo Building. Every seat is in a private room, some with sunken kotatsu, some at a counter, and dinner is a reservation-only omakase of many bite-sized seasonal dishes, with very fresh fish, good chicken and a sake list to match. Diners praise the variety and presentation; one was surprised by the konjac with roe. Portions are small, and two diners left wishing for more volume. Expect ¥10,000–20,000. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Private-room Japanese restaurant with a staff-maintained Tabelog listing (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Fish and seasonal vegetables from producers, the day's best in small plates (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "All the dishes are elegant and served in bite-sized portions, making it highly recommended for those who enjoy drinking… I was pleasantly surprised by the deliciousness of the konjac with roe appetizer…" — September 2026.
"It's on the first floor of the Nippo Jumbo Building, with the entrance facing Yahata Street, so look for the red sign…" — May 2026.

osaka_asakusa_chaya_tabanenoshi_shinsaib.notes: [Sweets · Kakegawa-matcha crepes from a Tokyo tea-house chain, Shinsaibashi] The Shinsaibashi branch of Asakusa Chaya Tabanenoshi, a Japanese-crepe chain from Asakusa, on Shimizu-machi-suji across from the Daimaru car park. Everything turns on Kakegawa matcha from Shizuoka: the signature Kakegawa matcha brûlée wraps matcha custard, strawberries and matcha ice cream in a chewy matcha crepe, then torches the top so it cracks. Seasonal versions rotate, such as an autumn Tsukimi brûlée (¥1,250); there's also hojicha with anko butter, matcha soft serve and lattes. You can watch them being made. Only about five tables, so on weekends it fills and takeout is the easy option.

chef_bio.origin: Osaka branch of Asakusa Chaya Tabanenoshi, a chain begun in Asakusa, Tokyo (official site; October 2026 review); opened 30 September 2024 (Tabelog).

chef_bio.philosophy: Kakegawa matcha from Shizuoka (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "The crepe itself seemed to have matcha mixed into the batter, making it very delicious and chewy… There were only about five tables, so the place filled up quickly…" — September 2026, Matcha Brulee Crepe.
"I was intrigued by the autumn limited 'Tsukimi Brulee'… JPY 1,250… The restaurant was fully packed, and there were several people waiting for takeout…" — October 2026.

Opened 31 May 2021 (Tabelog).
osaka_cafe_noone_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Café · a Korean-style dessert café for Dubai chocolate mochi, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A stylish, calm Korean-style café a few minutes from Shinsaibashi, with a terrace and a big glass case of desserts: grab a seat, then pick from the case. The draw is the Dubai chocolate mochi (¥740), chewy outside with pistachio and a crunchy filling, which often sells out (check the shop's Instagram stories). Also a crackly brûlée cheesecake with ice cream (¥980), strawberry-matcha and Earl Grey shortcakes, a pumpkin Basque cheesecake and bear-shaped sablés. There's another branch in Amerikamura with a slightly different menu. One diner waited a long time for an order; another found the cookies a little stale.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 31 May 2021 (Tabelog); a separate Amerikamura branch exists (March 2026 review).
chef_bio.background: Korean-style dessert café (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The Dubai Chocolate Mochi has a chewy exterior and a crunchy texture inside. The sweetness of the chocolate combined with the nuttiness of pistachios creates a completely new experience…" — March 2026, ¥740.
"The ordering process involves securing a seat first and then choosing from a delightful array of desserts displayed in a large showcase…" — March 2026.
